evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:720 `unresolvable = commit_impact.unresolvable_shas([r["sha"] for r in records], tracker)` then raises RebarError 'nothing was recorded' when non-empty
src/rebar/__init__.py:105 `attach_commits,` — the function is a public exported API surface

Consumer tests/interfaces/store/test_commits_on_ticket.py:27-28 attach `["abc123", {"sha": "def456", ...}]`; :39-40 attach `["a","b"]`/`["b","c"]`; :75 `["s1","s2"]`; :93 `["x","y"]` — all synthetic SHAs

tests/interfaces/conftest.py:108-121 `rebar_repo` is a real cloned git repo (`_clone_template(...)`), so `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}` on 'abc123'/'a'/'s1' returns non-zero → `unresolvable_shas` flags them → attach_commits raises, breaking these existing consumers
src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:invalid_commit_shas runs `git ... rev-parse --verify --quiet {sha}^{{commit}}` and appends any nonzero-exit sha to the invalid list
indeterminate.finding: The pre-existing public `rebar.attach_commits(ticket_id, commits)` API now rejects SHA strings that do not resolve to a real commit object in the repo (new `commit_impact.unresolvable_shas` validation), narrowing previously-accepted input on an already-shipped exported surface. Existing consumers that attach synthetic/arbitrary SHAs will now raise `RebarError` where they previously succeeded.
scenarios: Any existing caller of rebar.attach_commits() that passes a SHA not present as a commit object in the current clone (including the shipped interface test suite)
A CLI/MCP caller attaching a SHA that lives only in another clone (unfetched) — now rejected outright
